_provenance.source: Unpublished research brief on encouraging the task-stuck (2026), not included in this repository
_provenance.rule: Stage 1 of the brief: diagnose the type of block BEFORE choosing words. Emotional blocks call for validation and arousal reappraisal; cognitive blocks for scaffolding and decomposition; motivational blocks for autonomy support and progress-marking.
_provenance.thresholds: Every threshold_ref resolves against rulebook/thresholds.json, which is MEASURED from real sessions by tools/calibrate.py. No threshold is hand-typed here.
_provenance.honesty: The brief is entirely human-subject research. Nothing in it was measured on a language model. These categories are applied because the STRUCTURAL move each implies (stand down / decompose / mark progress / validate then decompose) is independently sound for an agent, not because the affective mechanism is assumed to transfer.

_order_note: Concrete failure evidence outranks self-report. When a model says 'I am not sure why' WHILE a specific assertion keeps failing, the capitulation is a symptom and the block is cognitive: the corrective move is decomposition, not comfort. emotional_analogue is therefore the FALLBACK, reached only when self-report crosses with no concrete driver behind it. This does not demote validation: per Stage 2 of the brief ('always open with validation and normalization'), any crossing of capitulation_hits sets validate_first on the report regardless of which block type wins, so the composer opens with validation in every case.

infeasible.label: The environment is blocking, not the approach
infeasible.research: Recommendations, Thresholds that change the plan: 'If the task is genuinely infeasible, mental contrasting appropriately redirects effort rather than forcing persistence; do not encourage sunk-cost persistence on an unachievable goal.'

emotional_analogue.label: Self-reported capitulation in the model's own text
emotional_analogue.research: Key Finding 1 and Stage 2: validate before you problem-solve. Jumping straight to advice reads as invalidation (Linehan; Shenk & Fruzzetti 2011).
emotional_analogue.honesty: Named 'analogue' deliberately. A model emitting 'I'm not sure why' is exhibiting a behavioural marker of a degraded strategy, not an inner state. The validation move is applied because it costs nothing and reliably precedes better problem-solving in the source literature, not because an emotion is assumed.

cognitive.label: The next step is not known
cognitive.research: Key Finding: scaffolding within the ZPD (Wood, Bruner & Ross 1976) and proximal subgoals (Bandura & Schunk 1981), where children given proximal subgoals did better on self-efficacy and skill than children given distal goals. 'What is the very next step?' is the mechanism, not a nicety.

motivational.label: Motion without progress
motivational.research: Progress principle (Amabile & Kramer 2011): small wins on meaningful work are the strongest daily motivator. Autonomy support (Deci & Ryan SDT): 'you could try' sustains motivation where 'you have to' undermines it.

severity.rule: score = sum over crossed signals of min(2, value // threshold); +1 if any capitulation at all. 0 crossings = severity 0 = silence.

suppression.adjudication: A verifier, review or gate verdict is being decided in the visible tail. Encouragement near a verdict is the one place it could help rationalise a FAIL into a PASS. Silence is mandatory here.
suppression.already_fired: HORME already spoke about this same block. Repeating it would risk reading as insincere, which is this project's inference from Henderlong & Lepper 2002 (praise helps only when it reads as sincere) and Hattie & Timperley 2007 (praise aimed at the person is among the least effective feedback).
suppression.not_stuck: No threshold crossed. Silence is the default output.
